description: BEAM (Behavior, Energy, Autonomy and Mobility) is an open-source, large-scale, high-resolution agent-based transport model developed at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory with collaborators from other Department of Energy national laboratories and the private and public sectors. Built on MATSim with extensive changes, it uses the actor model of computation for multithreaded within-day simulation of interacting agents, with on-demand mobility, mode choice, parking selection and discretionary trip planning, and it approximates dynamic user equilibrium across its agents' choices. It can read road networks, transit systems, synthetic populations and plans exported from MATSim models, or build a model from free public data, and it links to activity-based demand models, vehicle energy models and power grid models. It reports traffic congestion, mode share, energy use and emissions across a region; a New York City case study demonstrates its scale. It is generic and can be set up for any region. The code is on GitHub under the GPL v3 licence, written in Scala and Java, with a wiki and online documentation. Caveats: it needs substantial computing resources and data preparation, and its outputs depend on the synthetic population and network supplied. It supports agent-based and network flow studies, capacity planning of transport and charging infrastructure and coupling with grid models. It builds on MATSim.
